items.prompt: Which statement matches Python sorted(records,key=...) in this lesson?

options.text: It returns a new list, but its record objects can still be shared
options.why: Creating a new outer list is not a deep copy of nested records.

options.text: It mutates every record into a new immutable value
options.why: Sorting changes ordering, not every nested object.

options.text: It always returns None and changes the caller list order
It invents authenticated source ordering for equal keys
options.why: Stability only preserves the supplied relative ordering.

items.explanation: Separate outer-list ordering/ownership from the mutability of objects referenced by that list.
